narratives.Description: [framework-gap] Add a fail-closed observable UI scope contract for fields-only changes
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Add a fail-closed observable UI scope contract for fields-only changes

## Context

A consumer project using Directive 0.117.0 had several stories intended to align a backing data model and bound UI fields. The implementation also changed the selected and default tab, tab order, labels, controls, card hierarchy, and table structure. One story contained no requirement for a new default tab, tab order, or card layout. Another described a set of columns as suggested, but implementation tests hardened the full set as a fixed UI contract. Project authority assigned ownership of the affected views but did not authorize unconstrained presentation redesign. The ingested xBRIEFs had empty file_scope and intended-placement boundaries.

## Expected behavior

For any task touching a user interface, Directive should require an explicit observable-change contract that distinguishes data or field binding from copy, interaction, navigation, and layout changes. A fields-only contract should name allowed visible changes and preservation invariants such as existing tab names, order, default selection, headings, controls, table structure, and major containers. Pre-PR should fail when semantic UI structure or a UI test assertion changes outside that approved contract. Any structural delta should require focused human approval rather than being hidden inside approval of a long issue body.

## Actual behavior / gap

Current controls verify issue and xBRIEF freshness, lifecycle, approved intent digests, optional file scope, acceptance commands, tests, and diff hygiene. They do not compare observable behavior with an approved baseline. File scope cannot distinguish adding a field binding from rearranging navigation inside the same authorized HTML, JavaScript, or CSS file. If issue prose is already overbroad, scope provenance freezes the drift, and tests can turn an optional suggestion into an apparently valid requirement. The manual pre-PR scope check can identify scope creep but does not provide an independent, fail-closed oracle.

## Session notes

### Proposed first ship

Add a typed plan.observableChange object, or an equivalent schema-owned contract, containing:

- changeKind: fields-only, copy, interaction, navigation, layout, or mixed;
- baselineRef: the merge-base UI authority;
- allowedChanges: the complete approved set of observable changes;
- mustPreserve: observable invariants that may not change;
- designApprovalRef: required for interaction, navigation, layout, or mixed changes.

The existing intent-digest mechanism already pins unknown plan keys, so this contract should compose with scope provenance rather than create a second authority system.

### Deterministic enforcement

Add one verify:observable-scope check when configured UI paths change:

1. Require an observable-change contract and baseline reference.
2. Produce a semantic accessibility or DOM structure summary for the merge base and candidate.
3. Compare tab names, tab order, default selection, headings, controls, table columns, landmarks, and major containers.
4. In fields-only mode, fail on every unlisted structural delta.
5. Print one remediation: restore the baseline behavior or amend the scope through explicit human review.
6. Require every newly asserted user-visible invariant in UI tests to cite an approved acceptance-criterion ID. An untraced assertion fails.
7. Preserve RFC2119 strength: SHOULD, suggested, or example language must not become a mandatory UI assertion without a human-approved scope amendment.

### Slicing and refinement behavior

Before filing or activating UI work, present a compact review surface:

- Will change: exact observable deltas.
- Will remain unchanged: navigation, layout, interaction, and terminology invariants.

Child issues must inherit parent preservation constraints. Any child that introduces a new structural change without parent traceability becomes HITL and requires focused design approval.

### Acceptance criteria

- A fields-only story allowing three new bound fields fails if the implementation also makes another tab the default.
- The same story passes when only the approved fields and bindings change.
- A candidate fails if it reorders tabs, adds controls, changes heading hierarchy, or changes table columns without listing that delta.
- A UI test fails traceability when it pins behavior absent from approved acceptance criteria.
- Suggested or SHOULD wording cannot satisfy a mandatory test trace without an approved amendment.
- Layout-authorized work passes when every semantic delta is listed and has a design approval reference.
- Existing non-UI projects and UI-free changes are unaffected.

### Non-goals

- Pixel-perfect screenshot gating.
- Policing cosmetic CSS values.
- Treating all UI changes as human-gated.
- Replacing file_scope, scope provenance, or existing pre-PR review.
- Inferring product intent from generated tests.

Refs #1709.

### Comment by @dbcall2 (2026-09-13T20:14:44Z)

model: claude-opus-5
role: critic

Round 1, fresh critic, open critique. Pinned to `b9511febc28cd6d08e3280a0c5cd05f05e38b4bc`; id ceiling 5655777237 inclusive. Injection / swarm lens fires: the target introduces two new authority tokens (`designApprovalRef`, `baselineRef`) and a new baseline authority, so authority is in scope below.

## Anchors re-verified

| Claim | Method | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dispatch-sha is the origin default tip | `git fetch origin`; `git rev-parse origin/HEAD origin/master` | holds -- both resolve to `b9511feb` |
| round-1 ceiling is the triage write-back | REST `/issues/4495/comments`; write-back id vs recorded ceiling | holds -- 5655777237 is the write-back id |
| "intent-digest already pins unknown plan keys" | read `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/extract-intent.ts` at the pin | holds -- `classifyPlanPath` returns `unknown`, the subtree is copied wholesale into the preimage and recorded in `unknownPaths` |
| "current controls ... do not compare observable behavior" | inventory of `verify-*` surfaces + `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts` | partly false -- see S1 |
| the composition anchor fails closed | read `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts` and `packages/cli/src/verify-scope-provenance.ts` | false in the reported configuration -- see B2 |

Mechanisms inventoried before weighing new ones: approved-scope provenance and the `intent-extract-v1` preimage (#3145 / #3205 / #3385), `verify:evaluator-surface` and its closed `EVALUATOR_SURFACE_PATH_PATTERNS` list (#4386), gate integrity (#3156), typed acceptance evidence with the strict `observed_behavior` axis (#3240), `verify:consumer-test-lane`, `flagPassAfterFailWithMethodChange` (#3322), goal-gate determinism (#852), UAT.

I did not audit panel-deposit completeness: that comment sits above the ceiling.

---

## B1 -- both authority inputs are worker-declared `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** The first ship puts `baselineRef` and `designApprovalRef` inside `plan.observableChange`, i.e. inside the artifact the implementing worker edits. The existing answer to this exact shape is not composition with a digest: `content/docs/scope-provenance.md` takes authority from the record committed to the **merge base**, refuses agent-shaped stamps (`kind: agent`, `actor: agent:...`) as renewal or first-adoption authority, hard-fails an approval created or rewritten in the same change set, and mints only behind the #3110 human-presence gate (TTY, `--confirm`, typed phrase, agent/CI env markers refuse). `--actor` is documented as display-only and "never authorizes mint". Separately, `resolveDefaultBaseRef` in `packages/core/src/evaluator-surface/evaluate.ts` **computes** the base and returns an error rather than falling back -- it does not accept a declared ref.

**Failure mode.** A worker writes `changeKind: layout`, lists the deltas it just made under `allowedChanges`, and sets `designApprovalRef` to any issue URL. Step 5 passes. Acceptance criterion "Layout-authorized work passes when every semantic delta is listed and has a design approval reference" is then satisfiable with zero human in the loop, and the gate's fail-closed property is decorative. The `baselineRef` half is worse: a declared ref pointed at a revision that already contains the redesign yields an empty structural delta and a green run on any `changeKind`.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean cannot bind as written. Either `baselineRef` is computed (merge base, tool-resolved, error on unresolvable) and `designApprovalRef` resolves to a human-origin record on the merge base under the #3110 mint, or the design must state expressly that the gate detects drift and does not authorize it -- which contradicts "Any structural delta should require focused human approval".

## B2 -- the named composition anchor is warn-by-default in exactly the reported configuration `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** The issue's session notes rest the whole authority story on one sentence: "The existing intent-digest mechanism already pins unknown plan keys, so this contract should compose with scope provenance rather than create a second authority system." The pin holds (table above). The enforcement does not. `packages/cli/src/verify-scope-provenance.ts` parses `--enforce` and defaults it to `false`. `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts` computes `const hard = input.enforce || currentScope.length > 0`, and the soft-migration branch is gated on `!enforce` with an empty declared scope; the module header says "missing approved-scope records -> warn (exit 0) unless `--enforce`". The Context section of this issue records that the consumer's "ingested xBRIEFs had empty file_scope".

**Failure mode.** Empty `file_scope`, no base-committed digest, default invocation: `currentScope.length === 0` and `enforce === false`, so the finding is soft and the process exits 0. `plan.observableChange` rides that same path -- it is pinned into a preimage that nothing is required to compare against, in precisely the scenario that produced the report. The new gate then either trusts an unverified contract or duplicates the verification, which is the second authority system the issue says it is avoiding.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean cannot bind while its only stated authority anchor is advisory by default at the motivating configuration. The design has to name one of: `verify:observable-scope` requires `--enforce`-grade provenance as a precondition and hard-fails without it; or `observableChange` carries its own base-committed record; or the first ship is explicitly scoped to projects that have already adopted enforcing scope provenance.

## B3 -- no oracle is named, and the house precedent for an undeclared capability is skip, not fail `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** Step 2 asks for "a semantic accessibility or DOM structure summary for the merge base and candidate" and never picks between the two. The a11y branch needs a rendered tree: I grepped every `package.json` in the tree (root plus the four workspace packages) for `playwright|puppeteer|jsdom|cheerio|happy-dom|axe` -- zero hits; the only devDependencies are biome, `@types/node`, vitest + coverage, tsx, typescript. Every shipped `verify:*` evaluator I inventoried reads git text, JSON, or markdown. The source-parse branch is per-framework, and `content/languages/` carries 26 packs from Swift to VHDL. The nearest precedent is explicit: `packages/core/src/consumer-test-lane/evaluate.ts` documents "Absence is skip, not invention" and skips when no test command is declared, and `content/docs/gate-integrity.md` restates it -- "When nothing is declared, it skips -- it does not invent `go test ./...`."

**Failure mode.** Two branches, both bad. Fail-closed on a missing renderer hard-fails every UI-touching PR in every consumer without a headless-browser harness, and the acceptance criterion "Existing non-UI projects and UI-free changes are unaffected" does not cover a UI project with no harness -- there is no remediation to print except "install a browser". Skip-when-unavailable follows house precedent but means the gate is absent exactly where a project has no UI test infrastructure, i.e. where drift is least likely to be caught by anything else. Producing the merge-base summary also implies building and booting the app at two revisions inside a pre-PR loop, which no current gate does.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean cannot bind until it names the extractor, its input (rendered tree vs committed markup), and the behaviour when the extractor cannot run. "Fail-closed" is an unbacked claim while the oracle that would produce the failure is unspecified.

---

## S1 -- the control inventory omits two mechanisms, one of which already owns this gap by name `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** The gap section lists the current controls as "issue and xBRIEF freshness, lifecycle, approved intent digests, optional file scope, acceptance commands, tests, and diff hygiene". Two omissions. First, `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts` ships a closed evidence-kind set including `observed_behavior`, and `STRICT_ACCEPTANCE_AXES` makes `deploy`, `smoke`, `uat`, `observed_behavior` unsatisfiable by merge or review evidence alone, with human-origin disposition required -- that is an existing observable-behaviour authority, just not a deterministic differ. Second, `content/docs/gate-integrity.md` lists under its non-goals "Falsifiable oracles for derived acceptance clauses (separate acceptance-design gap)" and closes with "Falsifiable oracles for derived clauses stay a separate acceptance-design gap."

**Failure mode.** Neither is cited, so the arc records scope for a new mechanism without establishing that #4495 is not the UI-shaped instance of an already-named, already-deferred acceptance-design gap. If it is that instance, the first ship builds a parallel authority beside `verify:ac` -- the shape #3156's non-goals refuse ("A parallel history detector beside #3322") -- and #852's ratchet rule points the other way: when a pass is spurious, ratchet the existing gate rather than add one.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean can bind, but the recorded scope has to say whether this is a new axis or a ratchet of acceptance evidence, and cite the named gap. That changes what the first ship is, not whether one is warranted.

## S2 -- steps 6 and 7 are not decidable, and step 6 collides with the issue's own non-goal `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** Step 6 fails "every newly asserted user-visible invariant in UI tests" that does not cite an approved acceptance-criterion ID. Nothing in the tree classifies an assertion as user-visible: I checked the acceptance surfaces (`verify-ac/`, `literal-acceptance/`, `product-first-done-gate/`, `scope/acceptance-evidence.ts`) and evidence is a typed record with a free-text `pointer` -- there is no test-file parser and no AC-ID trace. Step 7 requires deciding that a given assertion was licensed by SHOULD/suggested/example prose rather than MUST prose; no shipped mechanism maps an assertion back to source modality. The issue's own non-goals include "Inferring product intent from generated tests".

**Failure mode.** A gate that must classify "user-visible invariant" either over-fires (every new `expect` in a file under the UI pathspec demands an AC ID, so ordinary test work needs scope amendments) or under-fires (only assertions matching a hardcoded matcher list count, and the redesign is asserted through one that is not on the list). Both are non-deterministic pass/fail, which `content/patterns/goal-gate-determinism.md` puts outside the rigid axis.

**Disposition consequence.** The lean can bind, but steps 6 and 7 should be split out of the first ship or restated as a decidable predicate -- e.g. "a test file under the UI pathspec whose diff adds assertions fails unless the plan lists the corresponding delta", which is decidable from the diff and needs no intent inference. Leaving them in as written makes the first ship's fail-closed claim rest on an undecidable classifier.

---

## Footnotes

- `footnote` -- `changeKind: mixed` is an unexercised escape hatch. Six of the seven acceptance criteria pin `fields-only` or layout-authorized behaviour; none fails a candidate that declares `mixed`. A worker that cannot pass `fields-only` can declare `mixed` and satisfy the listed criteria. No evidence yet that this is load-bearing rather than a drafting gap, so it is not classified higher.
- `footnote` -- Stop-1 recording is consistent, with a contract seam behind it. The write-back carries `refutation-target:` under `charter: open critique`, which is what `## Stop 1 -- Gate` requires unconditionally, and the dispatch envelope correctly omits it per the Stop 3 prohibition. `### The arc` nonetheless says "Open critique names no refutation target". Nothing here misfired; the seam belongs to the contract, not to this arc.

## Road not taken

I considered arguing for the opposite disposition: drop the new gate and ratchet `observed_behavior` acceptance evidence plus a preservation-invariant clause on the plan item, so preservation rides `verify:ac` and the strict-axis rule already refuses merge/review evidence for it. I did not lean that way because it inherits the human-throughput cost the issue is trying to remove, and because a preservation invariant expressed only as evidence still has no differ. That is S1's shape rather than a fourth blocking finding.

## Steelman, and what would flip the verdict

The strongest position against me: derived-clause oracles have been deferred in this repo for a while, a structural diff over committed markup is cheaper and more deterministic than a human UAT pass, and every objection above is about the first ship's mechanism rather than the gap being real. I accept the gap is real -- the Context section describes drift that no shipped control catches.

B3 flips if the design names an offline, no-render extractor over committed markup for a declared set of file types, with a published skip contract for undeclared projects. B2 flips if the first ship makes enforcing scope provenance a precondition, or lands `observableChange` in a base-committed record of its own. B1 flips if `baselineRef` becomes tool-computed and `designApprovalRef` resolves through the #3110 human-presence mint; a `designApprovalRef` that stays a plan-authored string does not flip it, because the failure there is self-authorization and not detection quality. I will not close any of the three on "a reviewer would notice the contract was self-written" -- that is the control this issue exists because it lacks.


### Comment by @dbcall2 (2026-09-13T20:16:16Z)

model: gpt-5
role: critic

Verdict: the reported gap is substantiated, but the lean cannot bind as written. It needs a successor lean that defines the oracle, its applicability, and its authority boundary before a fail-closed gate is credible.

## blocks-the-design — The proposed semantic comparison has no canonical observable-delta language

Evidence: at dispatch SHA `b9511febc28cd6d08e3280a0c5cd05f05e38b4bc`, `scope-provenance/evaluate.test.ts` deliberately passes when only `src/app.ts` changes and the active xBRIEF does not; that confirms the present mechanism protects approved-plan drift, not implementation behavior. `verify-ac/clauses.ts` likewise marks a behavioral claim without a real oracle as `unverifiable`. The issue proposes a “semantic accessibility or DOM structure summary,” but does not define a versioned output schema, stable surface/node identity, state/fixture enumeration, normalization, or how an `allowedChanges` entry matches one discovered delta.

Concrete failure mode: two equivalent renders can fail because generated IDs or wrapper nodes move, while an unauthorized interaction, route, default selection, or CSS-driven visibility change can pass because it is absent from the one rendered state. If the candidate can also change the extractor or normalization, it can erase the very delta being checked.

Disposition consequence: do not bind until the first ship defines a closed, versioned observable artifact (for example `observable-ui.v1`) with stable surface IDs, named states/fixtures, typed facts, and typed deltas. Base and candidate must be measured with the same base-authoritative provider/version and input set; missing, stale, invalid, or changed provider material must fail, with no generic fallback. `codebase/provider.ts` is useful prior art for schema validation, expected provider identity, freshness, content hashes, argv execution, timeout, and bounded output, but its fallback behavior is not safe for this gate. Because this adds automatic execution over repository-controlled UI inputs, the successor lean must also state the execution boundary (credentials/network, timeout/output bounds, and untrusted rendered content handling).

Road not taken: a single Directive-owned static DOM/AST extractor. Its strongest case is zero consumer configuration and an extractor the candidate cannot rewrite. It loses because static source cannot faithfully cover runtime state across server templates, React/Vue/Svelte, native/mobile, component libraries, routing, and CSS visibility. I would flip for a deliberately narrow first ship that names one supported representation and rejects every other UI stack rather than claiming “any task touching a UI.”

## blocks-the-design — Applicability is contradictory as written

Evidence: the target says both “for any task touching a user interface” and “when configured UI paths change,” while promising non-UI work is unaffected. No project-level UI-surface registry, config authority, missing-config result, or mixed-file rule is named. Existing `test-boundary/policy.ts` makes this choice explicit: configured policy enforces, inferred defaults warn. Existing `check/gate-lists.ts` and `consumer-check-contract/evaluate.ts` also show that a consumer fail-closed gate needs explicit aggregate/deposit composition, not only a new verb.

Concrete failure mode: treating absent UI configuration as N/A silently misses the incident class; inferring UI from extensions or directories false-fails non-UI changes and misses mixed data/UI files. A standalone `verify:observable-scope` can also remain green-but-unused if it is not in both framework and consumer check graphs and their integrity contract.

Disposition consequence: select and record one rollout contract. A defensible first ship is opt-in, base-pinned `observableUi.surfaces[]` policy: outside matched surfaces is N/A; inside a matched surface, an absent story-level observable contract fails. State honestly that this is not yet universal UI coverage. Add acceptance criteria for `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES`, `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES`, the required consumer enforcement set, Taskfile/deposit surfaces, and three-state missing/invalid configuration behavior.

## blocks-the-design — “Every newly asserted UI test invariant cites an AC ID” is not a deterministic cross-language gate

Evidence: current mechanisms have stable authored `plan.items[].id`, typed per-item evidence in `scope/acceptance-evidence.ts`, literal acceptance commands, and a clause walk. They do not inventory semantic assertions in arbitrary test languages; derived clause IDs in `verify-ac/clauses.ts` are local sequence numbers, and behavioral clauses without an oracle remain unverifiable.

Concrete failure mode: assertions hidden behind helpers, snapshots, parameterized tests, macros, custom matchers, or generated tests evade a syntax scan; a comment containing an AC ID can satisfy a shallow text scan without tracing the assertion. Conversely, requiring an inline marker on every assertion rejects legitimate helper-generated tests. Either outcome contradicts fail-closed traceability.

Disposition consequence: remove universal source-assertion scanning from the first ship. Put traceability on the typed observable artifact instead: every approved or discovered observable fact/delta names a stable authored requirement ID, and test results are evidence pointers for that ID rather than authority. If source-level assertion tracing remains desired, the lean must enumerate supported languages/frameworks and a real analyzer contract, with unsupported syntax failing explicitly.

## sharpens-framing — The proposed storage key conflicts with xBRIEF conformance

Evidence: `vbrief-validate/conformance.ts` excludes `observableChange` from `PLAN_CORE` and rejects every non-core bare plan key; `vbrief-validate/main.test.ts` demonstrates that a bare `customField` is a finding. `policy/plan-extensions.ts` records Directive-owned engine configuration under the `x-directive/` namespace. The targeted conformance and plan-extension tests passed on the dispatch tree.

Concrete failure mode: a brief containing `plan.observableChange` can satisfy the new verifier yet fail the existing `verify:vbrief-conformance` merge gate, or force an unrelated expansion of the xBRIEF core namespace.

Disposition consequence: retain the lean only with `plan["x-directive/observableChange"]` (or an equivalently namespaced Directive extension), unless this motion explicitly intends and justifies a change to the xBRIEF core standard.

## sharpens-framing — Preservation inheritance should compose with the existing parent-lineage protocol

Evidence: `scope/coverage-map.ts` already carries stable parent requirement IDs through closed dispositions and requires a linked `behavioral_delta` record for an intentional change; `scope/parent-lineage.ts` re-checks exact parent identity and fails on uncovered parent requirements and silently removed negative invariants. Those tests passed on the dispatch tree.

Concrete failure mode: a second UI-specific inheritance/approval graph can disagree with `parent_lineage`, allowing one gate to approve a structural delta while the other still treats the parent invariant as preserved.

Disposition consequence: give each `mustPreserve` fact a stable authored requirement ID and map child handling through the existing coverage-map / behavioral-delta path. Extend that path once at a namespaced storage boundary if UI-specific delta fields are needed; do not create a parallel child-inheritance authority.

## footnote — Protocol and anchor verification

The ceiling comment `5655777237` has the required lead, records `mechanism-shaped: true`, separates `charter: open critique` from `spend: N=3`, and names the no-ingest posture. The dispatch SHA resolves to both current HEAD and `origin/master`. I read no later comments. Across the relevant scope-provenance, acceptance, lineage, check-composition, provider, safety, policy, and conformance suites, 15 test files / 288 tests passed; the findings above are therefore about the current designed behavior, not red test residue.


### Comment by @dbcall2 (2026-09-13T20:18:09Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

Round 1, fresh critic. Charter: open critique. Spend: N=3 (panel permission used). Ceiling 5655777237 honored (issue body + triage write-back only). Re-derived at `b9511febc28cd6d08e3280a0c5cd05f05e38b4bc`. Process-only. No product patch.

The gap is real. Path scope, issue prose, and tests cannot see intra-file navigation or layout, so some fail-closed observable-change oracle is warranted. This lean cannot bind as written: it inherits the empty-scope skip that characterized the incident, does not name an oracle class that can witness its own default-tab criterion, and first-ships several unrelated surfaces as one check.

## Inventory (existing mechanisms, before any new one)

Measured at `b9511feb`, not cited from the issue:

| Need | What already exists | What it actually sees |
|---|---|---|
| Path authorization | `file_scope` digest + write fence | Sorted path list only (`computeFileScopeDigest` hashes joined paths). Same `src/App.tsx` after a field bind and after a tab-order rewrite produces the same digest. Empty `file_scope` → write fence falls back to project policy only. |
| Freeze approved intent | `intent-extract-v1` + `verify:scope-provenance` | Unknown `plan.*` keys are pinned wholesale (extract-intent tests, 50 passed including unclassified-key). Empty `file_scope` with no digest and `enforce: false` **warns and exits 0** (`evaluate.test.ts` "warns without failing for body-only modified xBRIEF with empty scope"). |
| Human-origin stamp | `scope:record-approved-scope` / #3110 TTY mint | Required for **non-empty** `file_scope`. Not required on the empty-scope class the issue reports. |
| Stated product checks | `verify:ac` / `plan.acceptance.commands` | Runs those command strings. Does not compare UI structure. Extra UI assertions are not refused. |
| Test placement | `verify:test-boundary` | Roots and basenames, not assertion-to-AC trace. |
| Pre-PR scope creep | pre-pr Phase 4 skill MUST | Prose review of `git diff`. No `task` oracle. |
| Intended placement | `#3424` `files[]` + size trigger | Path list and line-count, not tabs/landmarks. Missing field is grandfather-warn. |
| Visual / DOM | `content/interfaces/web.md` visual regression `~` | Not a check gate. `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES`, `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES`, `REQUIRED_CONSUMER_ENFORCEMENT_GATES`, and `dispatch.ts` have no `verify:observable-scope`. |
| Consumer gate composition | `REQUIRED_CONSUMER_ENFORCEMENT_GATES` (four names) | Adding a fifth required verb fails consumer Taskfile/CI until every deposit grows the graph. |
| One check, one remedy | named-cause + Thin Fail-Closed | Gate failures name one remedy string. |

`plan.observableChange` is not a known extract/machine key (`classifyPlanPath` default is unknown). xBRIEF 0.8 `additionalProperties: true`, so the object would parse and, **if minted**, pin as an unknown subtree. Pinning bytes is not evaluating them, and mint is what the incident skipped.

## Findings

### 1. Composing with provenance inherits the empty-scope skip, so the contract is self-authorizing on the incident class. `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** Re-ran `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.test.ts` at this SHA: empty `file_scope`, no approved-scope record, `enforce: false` → `exitCode === 0` and `WARN`. Non-empty `file_scope` without a digest hard-fails even without `--enforce`. Write fence: empty story `file_scope` → project policy only. The issue states the ingested briefs had empty `file_scope`. The proposed first ship says the new object should compose with intent-digest / scope provenance rather than a second authority system.

**Failure mode.** A fields-only story with empty `file_scope` never mints. The agent writes `changeKind: fields-only` and an `allowedChanges` list that matches the diff it already made (including the new default tab), or omits `mustPreserve`. Presence of the object satisfies a "require a contract" check. Provenance does not freeze a stamp that was never minted. Same-PR self-auth, the defect `#3145` already closed for paths.

**Disposition.** Do not bind until the observable-change object has a human-presence mint (`#3110` class, merge-base, same-PR rewrite fails) **when UI files change, including empty `file_scope`**. "Compose with provenance" is the pin format, not a license to reuse the empty-scope warn path.

### 2. The default-tab acceptance criterion has no named oracle class, and no shipped gate can witness it. `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** Proposed step 2 is "a semantic accessibility or DOM structure summary for the merge base and candidate." Shipped check lists contain no browser, a11y-tree, or DOM comparator (grep of gate-lists, required consumer gates, and `dispatch.ts` at this SHA: zero `observable` verbs). `verify:ac` runs command strings. Non-goal: pixel screenshots. The first acceptance criterion is: a fields-only story fails if implementation also makes another tab the default. Default selection in typical tab UIs is component state / `aria-selected` after render, not a static landmark in the merge-base HTML file.

**Failure mode.** An implementer takes the cheap static markup diff, the default-tab story stays green, and the filing incident recurs. Or they add a Playwright runner as a framework gate: new runtime class (bootable app per worktree, merge-base install, host display), with no existing consumer deposit for it. A checked-in a11y snapshot is the incident again (agent updates the snapshot in the same PR; product-oracle integrity `#3322` already forbids editing the comparison to go green).

**Disposition.** Do not bind until first ship names one deterministic oracle and the criteria that oracle can actually fail. If the oracle is rendered a11y-tree, say so and accept the runner cost. If it is static markup/JSX structure, drop or reslice the default-tab criterion to what that extractor can see. "Semantic summary" is not a method.

### 3. `designApprovalRef` as a string, and agent-authored `allowedChanges`, are untrusted authority. `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** Injection / swarm lens applies: new fail-closed authority, untrusted issue/xBRIEF input, shared plan schema, swarm children. The only shipped focused human approval for scope is TTY-gated mint, not a URL field. `requireHumanMerge` gates merge, not presentation deltas. Pre-pr scope creep is skill prose.

**Failure mode.** For `interaction` / `navigation` / `layout` / `mixed`, the agent sets `changeKind: mixed` and points `designApprovalRef` at the same overbroad issue (or any URL). Fields-only is bypassed without a new human presence event. In swarm, children with empty `file_scope` each rewrite the same view; proposed parent-preservation inheritance is skill text unless the mint is per-child and fail-closed. `allowedChanges` strings also flow into gate output / later envelopes (untrusted input).

**Disposition.** Do not bind a URL-shaped approval. Structural deltas, including a kind upgrade away from `fields-only`, need the same human-presence + merge-base stamp as approved-scope. Agent-written `allowedChanges` without that stamp is not a contract.

### 4. First ship stacks seven surfaces into one check. `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** Thin Fail-Closed prefers one fail-closed check and one remediation for a first ship. The issue already names one remediation for structural delta ("restore the baseline or amend through explicit human review"). Numbered steps 6–7 (UI-test AC trace, RFC2119 SHOULD/suggested/example must not become a mandatory assertion) need different remediations. Child inheritance and the slicing review surface are further surfaces. `commands.md` refuses free-text NLP as a gate classifier; RFC2119 strength in issue prose and test names is that class.

**Failure mode.** Implementer ships a wide red consumer gate, then weakens the oracle or the required-list to go green (gate-integrity pressure). Or the RFC2119 step becomes a prose classifier that both over-blocks and under-blocks.

**Disposition.** Bindable first ship is one check: human-minted allowed/preserve lists versus one named structure oracle, one remediation. Test-trace, RFC2119 strength, slicing review card, and child inheritance are follow-up issues, not this AC block.

### 5. "Configured UI paths" vs "any task touching a UI" vs required consumer composition. `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** Expected behavior: any task touching a user interface. Proposed check: when **configured** UI paths change. No `plan.policy` UI-path field exists at this SHA. AC also says non-UI projects and UI-free changes are unaffected. Putting `verify:observable-scope` on `REQUIRED_CONSUMER_ENFORCEMENT_GATES` (the `#3145` pattern) forces Taskfile/CI churn on every consumer; leaving it off means the filing class never runs it.

**Failure mode.** Opt-in config = the 0.117.0 consumer stays unprotected unless they know to configure. Required composition without an internal skip = non-UI repos go red. Unconfigured skip = the hole looks like a skip, not a fail.

**Disposition.** State a closed path classifier (or an explicit opt-in with warn-then-enforce, matching test-boundary) and whether the verb is required-composed with internal skip. The expected sentence and the trigger sentence must match before bind.

### 6. xBRIEF already accepts the object; visual regression is not a gate; intended-placement is not this oracle. `footnote`

Unknown-key pin and `additionalProperties: true` mean schema-owning `plan.observableChange` is not what closes the gap. `web.md` visual regression is a SHOULD, which the non-goal correctly refuses to promote. Intended-placement empty `files[]` is a size/path preflight, not tabs or landmarks. These do not change bind.

## Injection / swarm lens

Triggered (authority, untrusted input, shared plan/check state, swarm children). Findings 1 and 3 are the authority cases. Do not treat a long issue-body approval, a string `designApprovalRef`, or an agent-edited snapshot as the human gate. Close stdin/untrusted contract fields out of prompts; print ids and closed enums, not raw `allowedChanges` prose, in later envelopes.

## Road not taken

Rejected skill-only compact review: `#3265` already calls that incomplete when a gate can fail closed. Rejected "file_scope + prose + tests are enough": digest is path-list only (re-ran the stable-digest test); empty-scope provenance warns; `verify:ac` does not constrain extra UI assertions. Rejected checked-in screenshots: listed non-goal and `#3322`. The remaining fork is a human-minted closed-form delta list plus one derived (not checked-in) structure oracle, not the seven-step bundle.

## Steelman

Strongest rejected reading: a well-authored `file_scope`, an AC that says "do not change tabs," and tests that snapshot tab names would have caught this, so no new framework gate is due. What would flip that: the reported briefs had empty `file_scope`, did not authorize the presentation rewrite, and tests **held** the rewrite. Those three shipped controls failed together. That warrants a new oracle. It does not warrant binding this shape until mint, oracle class, and first-ship width are stated so the incident class actually fails closed.
